title: Poland's Energylandia to open new record-setting wing coaster in 2027
summary:
Energylandia, Poland's largest theme park, has announced a new record-setting wing coaster called Rokan for 2027.

Manufactured by Bolliger & Mabillard, Rokan will be the tallest and longest wing coaster in Europe when it opens next year.

The new attraction will reach a top speed of 115 km/h and a height of 62 metres. It will boast four inversions along a 1,215-metre-long track.

Rokan will be located in a new zone called Volana, which will open alongside the new coaster during the park's 2027 season.

"This extraordinary roller coaster features seats positioned on either side of the track, giving riders an incredible sensation of flying and an unparalleled feeling of freedom and space," said Energylandia.

"Rokan will be another spectacular milestone in Energylandia’s development."

Energylandia’s 20th roller coaster

Rokan will become Energylandia’s 20th roller coaster, setting a new world record for the most roller coasters at a single theme park.

Energylandia is already recognised by Guinness World Records for having the most roller coasters at one theme park. As of October 2026, the park has 19 active coasters, from family attractions to high-speed thrill rides.

See on Instagram

The two most recent additions to Energylandia's portfolio are a pair of family-friendly roller coasters called Choco Chip Creek and Honey Harbour.

The park's flagship attractions include Hyperion, one of Europe’s tallest and fastest coasters, and Zadra, a record-breaking hybrid coaster.

In an Instagram post, Energylandia said Rokan is taking shape and confirmed it will be ready for guests "as early as the 2027 season".

title: Six Flags Over Georgia reopens after fatal roller coaster incident
summary:
Six Flags Over Georgia has reopened after a man died and several others were injured in a roller coaster incident at the park last week.

Last Monday (12 October), 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem fell to his death after being ejected from his seat on the Goliath coaster. Authorities are investigating the fatal accident.

Six Flags Over Georgia was already scheduled to be closed on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday last week, and reopened as planned on Friday (16 October).

Park president Richard Pretlow confirmed the reopening in a statement. He wrote: "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences remain with the individual involved, their family, friends and loved ones."

Authorities investigate accident

"As efforts to understand the circumstances surrounding this tragic incident continue, we remain focused on supporting those affected and maintaining the safe operation of our park and attractions," Pretlow said.

"All other rides and attractions that were scheduled to operate will be available to guests, subject to normal operating conditions and availability."

Authorities and Six Flags have not identified the coaster involved in the incident, but witnesses told local media they saw a man falling from the park's Goliath ride.

Goliath is manufactured by Bolliger & Mabillard and opened in 2006. It boasts an elevation of 200 feet, a 170-foot plunge, and speeds of up to 70 mph.

Six Flags safety procedures

Pretlow said Six Flags Over Georgia maintains "rigorous inspection, maintenance and operational procedures that meet or exceed industry standards".

"Our attractions undergo daily, weekly, monthly and annual inspections, and our team members receive extensive training to safely operate and maintain our rides," he added.

"Each year, millions of guests safely enjoy the rides and attractions at Six Flags parks.

"While serious incidents of this nature are exceedingly rare, we never take responsibility to our guests for granted and remain committed to continuously strengthening our operations and safety practices."
